department: School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences

deadline.value: Traditional International Fall application deadline is January 15 (January 15, 2027 inferred for Fall 2027; Spring deadline September 15).
deadline.quote: Traditional International | Mathematics and Statistics with Interdisciplinary Applications Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Campus Based Jan 15 Sep 15 N/A N/A

english_waiver.value: Catalog states TOEFL 79 is required only if the medium of instruction in the bachelor's or master's program was not English (though UTRGV Graduate Admissions' country table lists India as requiring an English test—confirm waiver directly with the MSIA coordinator).
english_waiver.quote: TOEFL score of 79 or better for international students if the medium of instruction in their bachelors...program was not English.

gre_subject.value: Program admission requirements do not state whether a GRE Mathematics Subject Test is required or optional.

supervisor.value: Pre-admission supervisor agreement is not required; a track advisor or Graduate Program Coordinator advises initially while students explore advisors during their first year and Directed Study before choosing a dissertation advisor.
supervisor.quote: Initially, your track advisor or Graduate Program Coordinator may take this role. As you move closer to your dissertation stage, you will need to find a faculty member who will be your dissertation advisor. | Students should begin exploring possible advisors during the first year.

funding.value: Funding opportunities are limited and admission does not guarantee support; all admitted Ph.D. students are considered for GTA/GRA positions (0.5 FTE; minimum $1,250/month or $15,000/year for GTA/GRA, $2,400/month or $28,800/year for doctoral Associate Instructors, eligible for non-resident tuition waiver) plus College of Sciences Dean's Excellence Fellowships ($3,500/year) and travel grants.
funding.quote: School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences tries to provide funding to its graduate students, but the funding opportunities are limited. Admission to the PhD program in Mathematics and Statistics with Interdisciplinary Applications does not guarantee funding support. | The two most common sources of funding are Graduate Teaching Assistantships or Graduate Research Assistantships. All students admitted to the PhD program are considered for these two funding opportunities if available through the program.

also.quote: Assistantships give students the opportunity to work on campus (up to 20-hour work weeks). | Please visit with your graduate program director about the different assistantships available in your field of study. | careers.utrgv.edu for available graduate assistantship positions. | Eligible for Non-Resident Tuition Waiver: Yes | 10047 – Graduate Teaching Assistant $1,250 $15,000 $11,250 $3,750 | 10095 – Graduate Research Assistant $1,250 $15,000 $11,250 $3,750 | 10064 – Graduate Associate Instructor (doctoral level) $2,400 $28,800 $21,600 $7,200

entry_route.value: Admits both bachelor's holders (75 credit hours) and master's holders (57 credit hours) in STEM or related fields with at least 3 advanced undergraduate mathematics courses.
entry_route.quote: Students admitted with a bachelor...degree will complete a minimum of 75 hours to earn the PhD in MSIA

notes: Includes four official areas of emphasis: Computational and Applied Mathematics; Statistics, Data Science, and Machine Learning; Mathematical Methods in Natural and Applied Sciences; and Foundations of Mathematics with Applications. Requires personal statement, CV, and 3 letters of recommendation. Comprehensive exams may be exempted in up to one core course by earning an A grade.
name: Mathematics and Statistics with Interdisciplinary Applications (Ph.D.)
